name: Origami
visualIdentity: Explicitly defined by legible creases, facets, continuous paper, limited paper colors, and clean lighting. Origami folds follow defined creases in sequence; arbitrary 3D deformation is not origami.
suitableUses: Pure folding sequences, product or editorial introductions, illustrated explanations, and cinematic reveals. Tutorials benefit from crease diagrams that precede each fold; frontal staging can suit symmetric models. These are stated fits and suggested applications.
limitations: Do not stretch or split the sheet, allow self-intersections, or let paper pass through itself. Preserve connection and thickness. Avoid other paper deformations. Diagrams must match actual hinges and fold order; camera moves must not hide creases. Simulation alone does not establish valid origami behavior.
palette: Optional suggestion for new work: background ivory #F4F0E5, foreground #304347, terracotta #BA6F5C, sage #7C9A86. Use discrete tokens; gradients are disabled. These are not canonical colors. Exact task, brand, reference, and existing semantic colors take precedence; preserve material colors and role assignments. Accent 1 with background and accent 2 with foreground fail the stated normal-text contrast target, so keep body text on the main background or another existing contrasting backing.
motionAndInteraction: Model creases as mesh hinges; rig folds with parent-child transforms and validate fold order and self-intersections. Fold sequentially, then let the model settle before camera moves. For instructional HTML, pair SVG crease arrows with a prerendered fold clip and caption; provide previous/next and arrow-key controls, plus end states for reduced motion. Optional chapter/story progress can drive coordinated states; video schedules the same journey with timed reading holds. Ensure backward and direct seeks reproduce state.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience; honor supplied assets and explicit requirements. Sync audio with picture and inspect intelligibility, balance, clipping, and timing in the final output.
assetRequirements: Use connected, thickness-aware geometry divided along crease hinges, with defined fold targets and clean lighting. Diagrams must correspond to real hinges. Interactive examples may pair SVG diagrams, prerendered fold clips, captions, and a static reduced-motion state. Exact copy, assets, and audio are task-dependent or unspecified.
combinations: Use alone for pure folding. Style-109 crease-direction line art supports tutorials when it matches the rig exactly. Style-104 centered frontal staging can suit symmetric reveals; move the camera only after folds settle and preserve the symmetry axis and palette. These are suggested combinations, not requirements.
productionApproach: Blender with Python bpy owns geometry, materials, lighting, and authored folds; optional XPBD is only appropriate with crease targets, near-inextensible stretch, thickness-aware contact, and self-collision, and must be baked or deterministic. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, sync, validation, and export pipeline; Remotion is fallback only for unavailability or a verified limitation. Keep rendering and motion responsibilities distinct.
